ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the container on the left of the figure there are many identical gray circular particles, and they are dispersed throughout the whole container; the arrow points to the container on the right, and the particles in the right container still appear to be the same gray circular particles, only tightly piled at the bottom of the container. Then reason: a physical change only changes the state, shape, or arrangement of matter, and does not produce new matter; a chemical change will produce new matter or new particle types. In the figure, the particles themselves have not become different particles, but have only changed from being dispersed to being aggregated, so the composition of the matter remains unchanged, and therefore this is a physical change rather than a chemical change.

Therefore the diagram represents a physical change rather than a chemical change.
